title: Few-body bound states in the anyon-Hubbard model
authors: Isaac Tesfaye, Christina Mascherbauer, Joyce Kwan, Perrin Segura, Yanfei Li, Markus Greiner, Luis Santos, André Eckardt, Brice Bakkali-Hassani
abstract: Quantum statistics in low-dimensional systems predicts anyonic particles with fractional exchange statistics which are neither that of bosons nor fermions. While anyons are typically found in two dimensions as excitations of topologically-ordered states of matter, anyon-like exchange statistics has also been discussed in one dimension, for instance, in the context of the anyon-Hubbard model (AHM), the physics of which has recently been observed in experiment [Kwan et al., arXiv:2306.01737; Dhar et al., arXiv:2412.21131; and Bakkali-Hassani et al., arXiv:2602.20421]. The AHM can be formulated in terms of bosons featuring density-dependent Peierls phases, described by a statistical phase angle $θ$, which controls asymmetric transport and the formation of dynamically bound pairs at finite momentum. Here, we show theoretically that the AHM also hosts exact two-body bound states in the continuum (BICs) for arbitrary $θ\neq 0$, and genuine three- and four-body bound states. Unlike conventional bound states stabilized by attractive (or repulsive) interactions, which are energetically localized with a large effective mass, these clusters here are bound by a purely kinematic mechanism endowing them with fast chiral transport properties. We provide a simple variational approximation to the three-body bound states and explain their binding mechanism. Moreover, we show that the signatures of three-body bound states in the AHM can be directly probed experimentally from the expansion dynamics starting from three localized particles.
summary: This theoretical study investigates few-body bound states in the Anyon-Hubbard Model, a system modeling particles with fractional statistics. The authors demonstrate that these clusters are bound by purely kinematic effects, not just interactions, allowing for unique fast chiral transport. The findings provide a detailed theoretical roadmap for experimentally probing these exotic, strongly correlated quantum states.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates the existence and properties of few-body bound states (two-, three-, and four-body) within the Anyon-Hubbard Model (AHM). It specifically contrasts kinematic binding mechanisms with conventional energetic binding.
main_result: The AHM hosts exact two-body bound states for any non-zero fractional statistics angle $\theta$, and it exhibits genuine three- and four-body bound states. These clusters are bound by kinematics, enabling fast chiral transport.
method: The analysis involves mapping the problem to a single-particle problem on a relative coordinate space (triangular lattice) and employing variational approximations and exact diagonalization (ED) techniques.
model_or_system: The system is the Anyon-Hubbard Model (AHM), which describes particles with fractional exchange statistics ($\theta$). The Hamiltonian is formulated in a bosonic representation with density-dependent Peierls phases.
key_observables: Existence and nature of bound states (2-, 3-, 4-body), binding mechanism (kinematic vs. energetic), and signatures observable in expansion dynamics.
important_parameters: Fractional statistics angle $\theta$, on-site interaction $U$, and the quasimomentum $Q$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the problem to a single-particle Hamiltonian in the relative coordinate space and using variational methods for the three-body case.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the three-particle relative coordinate space, showing the lattice structure and colored regions indicating deeply bound 3-body (green) and 2-body (purple) states. Figure 2 shows the three-particle energy spectrum $E_Q$ vs. $Q$ for various $\theta$ values.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the AHM framework and the problem of few-body states. It then uses theoretical analysis and variational methods to prove the existence of kinematic bound states. Finally, it details the diagonalization of the relative coordinate Hamiltonian to characterize the different types of bound states (Type-I, Type-II, 3-body).
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from topological matter (anyons) and strongly correlated lattice models (Hubbard model), providing concrete, analytically derived predictions about novel quantum phases (kinematically bound clusters) that can be tested via time-of-flight expansion dynamics.
